uncited: *   **Input:** A sample point $P=(x,y,z)$ in 3D space; BS-AMR data consisting of bricks (typically $16 \times 16 \times 16$ cells) with cell-centered data values associated with refinement levels.
*   **Dual Cell ($D$):** A logical cell associated with the octant, used to determine vertex values via symmetry.
**Find Leaf Octant and Dual Cell:** Identify the leaf cell $C$ containing $P$ and its corresponding octant $O$.
**Compute Boundary Vertices:** For each boundary vertex (face, edge, corner), determine if it lies on a refinement boundary.
*   Face vertex $O(X)$: Average of two cells.
*   Edge vertex $O(XY)$: Average of four cells spanning the face.
*   Corner vertex $O(XYZ)$: Average of eight vertices of the dual cell.
*   **Fine Side:** If the current octant $O$ is on the finer level ($O.l > \min(\text{input levels})$), the vertex value is determined by the coarser side.
**Coarsest-Level Lerp:** Perform trilinear interpolation on the coarsest level involved for any of the inputs.
**Current-Level Lerp:** Perform trilinear interpolation on the current level.
**Basis Function:** Use a basis function interpolation.
*   **Recursion Depth:** The recursive call for fine-side vertices must terminate.
